reviewContext: President-authorized integration of Computational Irreducibility, incremental/delta computation, content-addressed structural sharing, probabilistic prefilters, Merkle integrity proofs, structural/dictionary compression candidates, multidimensional locality/indexing candidates, deterministic fleet placement, sparse representations, change-point sensing, adaptive checkpointing, memoized result reuse and cost-based execution planning into existing kernel governance and the self-diagnostic roadmap without creating live runtime services or touching Supabase
reviewedSemantics: the kernel now distinguishes Computational Irreducibility from Causal and Structural Irreducibility: a result should not be fully recomputed when a verified causal delta, immutable shared prefix, content-addressed prior result, safe candidate reduction or smaller equivalent computation is sufficient
the four optimization questions are now memory irreducibility, structural irreducibility, computational irreducibility and minimum sufficient disclosure
incremental computation is permitted only when dependency and invalidation semantics are mechanically proven for the affected result

counterfactual branches and other immutable worlds should share identical content-addressed prefixes/substructures rather than duplicate them, while semantic identity includes all required law/state/version/runtime meaning
deterministic memoization/result reuse requires complete law, state, input, runtime/numeric-contract and algorithm-version identity plus correct invalidation

probabilistic sketches such as Bloom/Count-Min/HyperLogLog/quantile sketches are treated as sensors, prefilters or explicitly approximate outputs rather than canonical truth where exactness is required
Merkle roots/proofs are treated as commitment or membership/integrity evidence and explicitly not as proof that the underlying fact is semantically true

delta, dictionary and grammar compression are candidate representations for repeated structures but must preserve exact reconstruction and beat mature compression baselines before canonical replacement

Hilbert/Morton space-filling curves, LSH/MinHash/ANN candidate generation and other locality indexes are candidate optimizations only after workload benchmarks and declared recall/false-negative semantics
consistent/rendezvous hashing may derive placement/partition without giant maps but does not define canonical entity identity
sparse matrices, compressed bitmaps and succinct exact sets are preferred candidates where dense empty/false state is wasteful, subject to benchmark against mature storage/index baselines

streaming change-point methods are sensors for possible information boundaries and cannot justify loss of required irreversible evidence until missed-change behavior is bounded for that information class
checkpoint density becomes a measured storage-versus-replay/recovery/latency trade-off rather than a blind fixed interval
the approximate-first exact-last pattern is allowed for candidate reduction only under an explicit recall/error contract and exact final verification where exactness is required

the future execution planner must enforce correctness, causal/replay, privacy/disclosure, provenance and recoverability constraints before minimizing CPU, storage IO, network, latency, energy, money or AI calls
Mission Gate now hard-blocks lossy probabilistic sketches or undeclared approximate outputs being used as canonical truth where exactness is required

Mission Gate now requires review for unknown incremental dependency semantics, cache identity/invalidation, approximate-prefilter false-negative behavior, change-point false-negative risk or misuse of Merkle proof semantics

Mission Gate now emits optimization guidance for unnecessary full recomputation, duplicate immutable branch prefixes, repeated deterministic computation despite a valid content-addressed result, full exact scans before safe high-recall prefilters, dense set storage, blind fixed checkpoint intervals, unbenchmarked custom locality/sketch methods and resource-ignorant execution plans

Mission Gate self-test expanded from 11 to 16 cases and review run 33691697850 executed syntax, KERNEL_HANDSHAKE and MISSION_GATE checks with zero added/deleted protected files and zero unclassified executable files; MANUAL_REVIEW_REQUIRED was the expected governance response to protected semantic drift

the self-diagnostic roadmap preserves all discussed candidate algorithms as future organs/comparison baselines rather than claiming they are implemented or superior to mature database/cache/index/compression/distributed-system techniques
no new production algorithm service, database schema, live dependency graph, cache, sketch, index, change-point detector, execution planner or Supabase write path was created by this transition
PostgreSQL/Supabase was not modified; cryosleep and all post-recovery backup, audit and handshake gates remain authoritative
